To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cadmium ion (Cd2+) induces spontaneous action potentials and contractions in the mouse diaphragmatic muscle, and that these actions of Cd2+ are mediated by increased Na+ permeabilty of the muscle membrane.
cadmium ion (Cd2+) has stimulatory effects on skeletal muscle, and that these effects involve the induction of spontaneous action potentials and increased sodium permeability.
Cd2+‐stimulated muscle contractility in the phrenic‐diaphragm preparations of the mouse, and this effect is related to increased Na+ permeabiliy of the muscle membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cadmium ion (Cd2+) on the mouse diaphrags.
the stimulatory actions of Cd2+ and its possible mode of action on the phrenico‐diaphragm muscle of the mouse.
the mechanism underlying the mode of stimulatory actions induced by Cd2+ on skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cd2+ has two modes of actions, i.e. inhibitory and stimulatory, and the latter is due to increased Na+ permeabilty.
Cd2+‐stimulated muscle contractility is a consequence of the depolarization of the muscle membrane.
Cd2+ induces myogenic activity in low Ca2+, low Na+ and high Mg2+ media by binding to ‐SH groups on the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd2+ has a stimulatory action on the muscle membrane, which is mediated by the binding of Cd2+, probably to the ‐SH groups of membrane proteins.
Cd2+ has a stimulatory effect on the muscle fibre membrane in the low Ca2+ concentration medium, and that this effect is closely related to an increased Na+ permeabiliy of the muscle fibre membrane.
the stimulatory effects of cadmium ion are mainly due to the increase of the membrane Na+ permeability.

the effects of Cd2+ are complex and depend on the experimental conditions.
